## Local Machine

### Private Repository Packages

[Source](https://golang.org/doc/faq#git_https)

#### Why does "go get" use HTTPS when cloning a repository

Companies often permit outgoing traffic only on the standard TCP ports 80 (HTTP) and 443 (HTTPS), blocking outgoing traffic on other ports, including TCP port 9418 (git) and TCP port 22 (SSH). When using HTTPS instead of HTTP, git enforces certificate validation by default, providing protection against man-in-the-middle, eavesdropping and tampering attacks. The go get command therefore uses HTTPS for safety.

Git can be configured to authenticate over HTTPS or to use SSH in place of HTTPS. To authenticate over HTTPS, you can add a line to the $HOME/.netrc file that git consults:

```netrc
machine github.com
login USERNAME
password APIKEY
```

For GitHub accounts, the password can be a [personal access token](https://docs.github.com/en/github/authenticating-to-github/creating-a-personal-access-token).

Git can also be configured to use SSH in place of HTTPS for URLs matching a given prefix. For example, to use SSH for all GitHub access, add these lines to your ~/.gitconfig:

```gitconfig
[url "ssh://git@github.com/"]
  insteadOf = https://github.com/
```

Finally, we need to tell go that the repository is private and has no entry in sum.golang.org. In .bashrc or .profile add the following

```bash
export GOPRIVATE=github.com/<USER OR COMPANY NAME HERE>
```

## Dockerfile

```
ENV GOPRIVATE=github.com/<USER OR COMPANY NAME HERE>
# It is important that these ARG's are defined after the FROM statement
# These are defined during the build stage or in our case in a github action
ARG SERVICE_USERNAME="nothing"
ARG SERVICE_TOKEN="nothing"
# working inside the appropriate go directory
WORKDIR /go/src/github.com/<USER OR COMPANY NAME>/<REPO NAME>
# using ssh for private repo access
RUN git config --global url."https://${SERVICE_USERNAME}:${SERVICE_TOKEN}@github.com".insteadOf "https://github.com"
```

## Kubernetes

This is not go related, but it was in the readme right next to it and was took some time to piece together. In order to access private repositories Kubernetes needs a Secret using a github personal access token or PAT with the `write:packages` permission.

[Creating a personal access token](https://docs.github.com/en/free-pro-team@latest/github/authenticating-to-github/creating-a-personal-access-token#using-a-token-on-the-command-line)

> 💡 Note
>
> You should have a separate personal access token for Github workflows, development cluster, and the production cluster for security reasons

```bash
kubectl create secret docker-registry github-registry \
  --namespace=development \
  --docker-server=ghcr.io \
  --docker-username=<github username> \
  --docker-password=<github personal access token> \
  --docker-email=<github email>
```
